title: GT_book (1)
universal_lens: Ordinal strategic-form games unify player preferences and rationality through dominance and Nash equilibrium concepts. Strategic form representation of extensive games with imperfect information and Bayesian updating under common knowledge assumptions.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models player belief updates using ordinal dominance hierarchies and Nash equilibria as posterior constraints. Bayesian belief revision functions map prior plausibility orders to posterior beliefs via AGM axioms in knowledge-based decision frameworks.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions in game dynamics are encoded via iterated strict dominance and equilibrium selection mechanisms. Situationally grounded state transitions model sequential decision-making under uncertainty using information sets and subgame perfection criteria.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter window systematically develops the epistemic foundations of solution concepts in game theory. It establishes that the procedure of iterated deletion of strictly dominated strategies can be justified as the consequence of common knowledge of rationality (CKR). The key insight is that for any surviving strategy profile, there exists a model where all players are rational and know each other's rationality ad infinitum. This bridges the gap between normative reasoning (rationality) and observable outcomes (surviving strategies). The analysis extends to sequential games via sequential rationality and Bayesian updating, providing a unified treatment of both static and dynamic settings. The challenge of weak dominance remains open, highlighting the fragility of solution concepts when indifference is involved.
